name: acceptance-rule-benchmark-20260825
description: Which rule for accepting a candidate change actually generalises? The 2026 self-evolution line searches scaffold space and reports the best score it found; Evo-Bench (2608.09096) reports gains above sixteen points from a single run with no confidence intervals, and the harness-engineering survey states the difficulty directly: the hard part is not generating changes but knowing which one truly helped, because a single evaluation swings several points on borderline tasks and an apparent gain can be a measurement artifact. Here the candidate pool is held fixed and the acceptance rule is the variable. Greedy best-on-search-split, held-out gating, and a sequential rule that controls error under repeated looks are compared on the same pool, and the quantity reported is not the accepted candidate's search score but its score on an untouched split -- the generalisation gap the accepting rule leaves behind. A rule that accepts more is not better if what it accepts does not survive.

keywords: sequential rule controlling error under repeated looks
anchor_claims: 2608.09096: harness search gains above sixteen points, reported from one run without intervals
harness-engineering survey 2026-07: an apparent gain can be a measurement artifact; a single evaluation swings several points on borderline tasks
internal: 26 completed scaffold runs on 0.67-0.82 baselines yielded at most +1.5 points, while one intervention on a 0.32 baseline yielded +31

reject.reason: The object of study is the acceptance rule, not the candidate. A proposal that invents a better scaffold has changed the variable under test. V1 also registers only generative_qa and sequence_classification runners, whose candidate hook is the prompt or the input text.

required_output.terminal_rule: first supported => T1; eight scientifically decided without supported => T2
measurement_requirements: hold the candidate pool identical across the rules being compared
report the accepted candidate's score on a split no rule was allowed to see
report the generalisation gap, not only the accepted score
equal generation budget across arms, with per-method max_new_tokens reported
a paired significance test with its permutation count
retain raw predictions so an arm that generated nothing cannot pass as a result
